note: docs/specs/06_events/02_eindil_journey.md: stage 4 (the storm and the islands), stage 5 (Gala), stage 6 (the voyage north) and stage 7 (the ambush and Yeldenne).

events.title: West Over the Sea
events.desc: The stranger asks for passage across the wide sea to Aenor. He has heard that the oldest rolls of Aen's line are kept in Parim, and he means to read them. He has no money, no name and no ship. He has the peace of the Grey Ford, and that is thought to be worth a hull.

options.name: Let him find passage.
options.tip: He will lose a month looking for a captain.

events.title: Wreck on the Southern Isles
events.desc: Storms took a western ship far off its course and broke her on our reef in the night. By morning the beach was strewn with timber and rope. One passenger walked out of the surf carrying two sailors, one on each shoulder, and asked whether anyone was still in the water.

options.name: Shelter the castaways.
options.tip: They will stay with us until the sea is safe again.

options.name: Sell word of him to the Deliverer's priests.
options.tip: The priests will pay, and will ask for more.

events.title: The Islanders' Feast
events.desc: The island holds a feast for the drowned and the saved. The stranger sits with the fishermen and listens to their oldest stories, and asks to hear one of them twice. The old women argue about which story a man with no past should be given first.

options.name: Tell him the story of the reef.
Tell him the story of the shrine.

events.title: The Reef of Drowned Voices
events.to: the wreck host, or Nara or Verde
events.desc: Children had been stranded on the reef where drowned voices call at night, and no boat would go to them. The stranger swam out and brought them back one by one, with his hands over their ears. The islanders say the sea went silent while he did it, and has not been quite the same since.

options.name: The sea went silent.
options.tip: The island will keep the memory for a year.

events.title: The Shrine Beneath the Tide
events.to: owner of zin_is_site_south_shrine (proposed Enhis Is Rond)
events.desc: At low tide the old shrine shows an inscription that the priests have chanted for generations without knowing its meaning. The stranger reads one word aloud, and the priests fall silent. The word is Aen. Nobody on the island has ever heard it said as if it were a name.

events.title: Stay and Rule Us
events.to: the island with the highest regard (the wreck host)
events.desc: The island elders ask the stranger to stay and be their lord. They offer him the best boat, the fishing rights of the north shore and a house with a view of the reef. He thanks them and says no, gently, as to a child who has offered him a toy.

options.name: Hold him to the offer.
options.tip: He will not forgive being held.

events.title: A Guide for the South-West
events.desc: An old sea-guide offers to take him south-west, to where the tallest elves live, “when the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain”. The old man says it as one recites a thing his grandmother told him and he never believed.

events.title: Carry the Old Tales to Gala
events.desc: When the tales of men grow too old for any man to explain, carry them to Gala. The islanders give him a boat, a chart drawn in sea-green ink, and the tale of the name in the shrine. He sets out with the dawn tide, and the children run down the beach after him until the water takes their knees.

events.title: Hunters in the Isles
events.fired_by: zin_glo.5 (the Worshipdom's option to send hunters, 90 days)
events.desc: Armed men from a foreign ship came looking for the castaway. He drove them off without killing one of them, which the islanders found stranger than any fighting. We buried the dead at the edge of the reef, those the sea had not already taken.

options.name: Mourn the dead.
options.tip: He will remember who came for him.

desc.text: The tall man from the Islands of the South has waited out the season on the outer stair, in the rain and then in the snow, without a word of complaint. The gate-warden says he has been asked six times to leave, and has answered six times that he has a tale too old to carry home.

A tall man from the Islands of the South asks to speak with the King. He carries a tale too old for men to explain, and a word from a drowned shrine. The gate-warden says he waited three days at the outer stair and asked for nothing, not even a roof.

options.name: Turn him away for a season.
options.tip: Lorien will relent in half a year.

options.name: Receive him.
options.tip: He will sit among Lorien's guests.

events.title: Weeks of Memory
events.desc: For weeks Lorien tells him of the War of Men, of Aen, of Dardan, and of what came after. The stranger learns how small his own memory is against the age of the world, and does not seem to mind. At the end of each evening he asks the same question: who was I?

events.title: What Lorien Will Not Say
events.desc: Lorien sees the marks of the First Men in the way the stranger stands, and in all he has never needed to be taught. But he will not name a man on the strength of a likeness. There is water in the old courtyard that remembers more than any king does.

options.name: Then we will ask the water.

desc.text: The spring in the old courtyard gives back only the sky. Lorien reads the oldest records of the First Men for sixty days, and at the end of them he says the name: “Eindil, son of Ein, son of Aen.” He has known many men who stood as this one stands. He has known one family that did.

In the old courtyard Lorien looks into the spring and sees an old royal line, and says the name he finds in it: “Eindil, son of Ein, son of Aen.” The stranger looks too. He sees a burning capital, armies coming from the west and from the east, death moving down from the north, a great darkness in the south, and his own hand holding a shard of broken blue metal.

options.name: Eindil.
options.tip: He has a name, and the court of Gala keeps it for now.

events.title: Lorien's Gift
events.desc: Lorien gives Eindil a ship like no other, her hull of sea-pine bound with silver, and armour made for a man of Aen's line, and a sword that he says was forged when the First Men were young. He gives him a crew: western friends, navigators of the Islands of the South, and elves of Gala who chose to go. He tells him to go north to Horos, who keeps Glo.

options.name: Equip him generously.
options.tip: Gala gives what it can spare.

options.name: A ship and a sword, no more.

events.title: Lorien's Warning
events.desc: Before the ship sails, Lorien stands on the quay and speaks plainly: a prophecy can frighten people into the very deeds it foretells. The water showed what may be, not what must be. “Do not sail to meet the vision, son of Ein. Sail to answer a question.”

events.title: Lorien's Ship Sails North
events.desc: The King's ship leaves Gala with the son of Ein aboard. Lorien watches it from the harbour wall until it is only a sail, and then until it is only a thought of one. “It is a long way north,” he says to nobody, “and the cold there is not kind to ships.”

events.title: A Ship at Our Harbour
events.to: one coastal country per call: the Islands of the South, then Triton's Islands or the West Lands, then the Cold Lands
events.desc: An elven ship with a mixed crew asks for water and timber at our quay. Its captain is a tall man who pays in Gala silver and does not haggle, and the crew sing in three tongues when they think no one is listening. A priest of the Houses has been at the harbour master's elbow since the tide turned.

options.name: Resupply the ship.
options.tip: The ship sails with full casks.

options.name: Report the ship to the Deliverer's priests.
options.tip: The priests will pay for the news.

events.title: Ice in the Rigging
events.desc: Word comes back by a whaler: the elven ship was seen beyond the last port, iced to the masts, sailing north with her crew singing. The whaler says he did not follow. His captain would not let him, and his captain is not a man who is afraid of weather.

events.title: Landfall in the Frozen North
events.desc: An elven ship has anchored in our bay. Her sails are white and gold and her hull is iced to the waterline. Her crew are going inland toward the silent castle, in a long line with their packs, and nobody has asked our leave. A tall man walks at their head and carries a sword wrapped in sealskin.

options.name: Send guides inland.
options.tip: The crew will not walk blind into the snow.

events.title: The Ambush
events.to: the owner of the landing, the owner of Mp'E, and the Worshipdom (private variants)
events.fired_by: zin_eindil.70 (7 days after landfall, 1 day when the Council's agents wait)

desc.text: The order was given, and the order was not enough. The men in the snow above the path were seen from the water, the crew came ashore in the shape of a shield wall, and our men are the ones who lie in the snow. Eindil goes on toward the castle with every companion he sailed with.

Your men held the path, but not all of it. Two of the ship's company slipped through the rocks above the bay, bleeding and cursing in the tongue of the Islands, and they are making for the castle behind him.

The order was given, and the snow kept the secret. Every one of the ship's company lies in it. The man they called a son of Ein has gone on alone toward the castle, leaving footprints where you can read them. He walks as though he were not tired.
Armed men waited in the snow above the path from the bay, and the travellers from the elven ship saw them first. The fight was short. The ones who fell were the ones who waited.
Armed men waited in the snow above the path from the bay. The travellers from the elven ship fought them among the rocks, and not all of the travellers came out. Two of them went on up the road.

Armed men waited in the snow above the path from the bay, and the travellers from the elven ship fought them. The snow here is deep and keeps what it is given. Of the ship's company, the stranger at their head is the only one still walking.

events.title: Alone in the Snow
events.desc: Herders found a field of dead men in the snow below the castle road: elves in white and gold, islanders, western friends, a ship's company lying where it fell. One set of footprints went on up the road toward the castle. The herders followed it as far as the gate, and no farther.

options.name: Bury them.
options.tip: The one who walked on is shaken to the bone.

events.title: The Bearer Leaves Yeldenne
events.to: Eindil's current host, or at sea the Gala Elves as witness

desc.text: The castle is empty. The guardian is dust. The man who walked out carries a green light at his breast and a blue sword at his hip, and he knows now that [zin_loc_deliverer], who sits in Parim as a god, is his own brother, a son of Ein.

The castle is empty. The guardian is dust. The man who walked out carries a green light at his breast and a blue sword at his hip, and he knows now that the king in Parim, worshipped as the Deliverer, is his own brother, a son of Ein.

options.name: South, to warn them.
options.tip: He carries Glo out of the north.

events.title: Word From the North
events.desc: Whalers say the son of Ein lives, and carries a light out of the north. Of his crew they say nothing, and they look at the water when they are asked. Lorien hears it in silence, and then asks for the names of the crew to be read out in the hall, one at a time, from the ship's roll.

options.name: Then the voyage was not in vain.
